original_question: Let {B X_m}_{m in N} be a direct system of classifying spaces of p-local finite groups with maps f_m: B X_m -> B X_{m+1}, and suppose the homotopy colimit hocolim_m B X_m is homotopy equivalent to B X for a p-compact group X. Must there exist some stage m and a map g-hat: B G_p-complete -> B X_m, where B G_p-complete is the p-completed classifying space of a finite group or of a p-local finite group, such that the induced map from B G_p-complete to B X factors the given map to B X up to homotopy through that stage?
target_in_paper: Section 1, Question 1.2, the "possibly related" question following Question 1.1. ([msp.org](https://msp.org/gtm/2007/11/gtm-2007-11-020s.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft is very close to the paper's actual question: it correctly uses a direct system {BX_m}_{m∈N} of classifying spaces of p-local finite groups, transition maps f_m: BX_m → BX_{m+1}, the hypothesis hocolim_m BX_m ≃ BX with BX the classifying space of a p-compact group X, and the desired conclusion that a map from a p-completed classifying space BG_p^∧ should factor up to homotopy through some finite stage BX_m. It also correctly preserves the paper's allowance that BG_p^∧ may come from either a finite group or a p-local finite group. ([msp.org](https://msp.org/gtm/2007/11/gtm-2007-11-020s.pdf))
missing_details: The paper states the problem relative to a specified map g: BG_p^∧ → BX; the sought map ĝ: BG_p^∧ → BX_m must make the displayed triangle homotopy commutative with that given g. Your draft alludes to this, but does not explicitly introduce the map g as part of the data. ([msp.org](https://msp.org/gtm/2007/11/gtm-2007-11-020s.pdf))

The quantifiers should be explicit: for a direct system as above, and for a map g: BG_p^∧ → BX, does there exist some index m and some map ĝ: BG_p^∧ → BX_m with the required homotopy-commutative factorization? ([msp.org](https://msp.org/gtm/2007/11/gtm-2007-11-020s.pdf))
The target space BX should be identified exactly as the classifying space of a p-compact group X, not just an arbitrary p-complete space. ([msp.org](https://msp.org/gtm/2007/11/gtm-2007-11-020s.pdf))

The source BG_p^∧ should be identified exactly as the p-completed classifying space of a finite group, with the parenthetical extension in the paper that one may also take a p-local finite group. ([msp.org](https://msp.org/gtm/2007/11/gtm-2007-11-020s.pdf))

The factorization condition is not merely that some induced map factors; it is specifically that the map g be homotopic to the composite BG_p^∧ → BX_m → BX given by ĝ followed by the canonical map from the m-th stage into the telescope and the chosen equivalence hocolim_m BX_m ≃ BX. ([msp.org](https://msp.org/gtm/2007/11/gtm-2007-11-020s.pdf))

Section 1 frames Question 1.2 as motivated by Broto-Møller's construction of direct systems of p-local finite groups approximating certain 1-connected p-compact groups; that contextual motivation is implicit in your draft but is part of the paper-faithful scope. ([msp.org](https://msp.org/gtm/2007/11/gtm-2007-11-020s.pdf))
refined_question: Fix a prime p. Let {BX_m}_{m∈N} be a direct system of classifying spaces of p-local finite groups with continuous maps f_m: BX_m → BX_{m+1}, and suppose that hocolim_m BX_m ≃ BX, where BX is the classifying space of a p-compact group X. Given a map g: BG_p^∧ → BX, where BG_p^∧ denotes the p-completed classifying space of a finite group G (or, as allowed parenthetically in the paper, of a p-local finite group), must there exist an index m and a map ĝ: BG_p^∧ → BX_m such that g is homotopic to the composite BG_p^∧ → BX_m → BX induced by the direct system; equivalently, can g be made to factor through some finite stage BX_m in a homotopy-commutative triangle? ([msp.org](https://msp.org/gtm/2007/11/gtm-2007-11-020s.pdf))
justification: The draft is targeting Section 1, Question 1.2 rather than Question 1.1. The distinctive features of your draft—a direct system of classifying spaces of p-local finite groups, a homotopy colimit identified with BX for a p-compact group X, and the request that a map from BG_p^∧ to BX factor up to homotopy through some stage BX_m—match Question 1.2 essentially verbatim. Question 1.1, by contrast, asks a different but related question: whether every p-compact group is itself a telescope of finite groups. The surrounding paragraph in Section 1 supplies the intended motivation from Broto-Møller's approximations of 1-connected p-compact groups by telescopes of p-local finite groups. The paper does not give an equivalent reformulation of Question 1.2 beyond the displayed homotopy-commutative diagram, so no alternate formulation should be added. ([msp.org](https://msp.org/gtm/2007/11/gtm-2007-11-020s.pdf))
